morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with growth form and fruit: an upright gray-green subshrub with ovate cordate leaves, small yellow flowers, and a compact cask-shaped schizocarp whose mericarps are only acute/apiculate rather than dramatically long-beaked.
diagnostic_traits: erect stellate-tomentulose stems without long simple hairs

confusers.separator: A. theophrasti is a tall annual with very large velvety heart-shaped leaves and a much larger wheel-like fruit with many long divergent beaks.
A. incanum has smaller reflexed yellow/pink flowers often with a dark red center and only five style branches.

photo_candidates.role: habit + gray velvety leaves + yellow flower

evidence_basis: Hays — UT Purola Preserve natural flora records Abutilon fruticosum.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Malvaceae specimen index documents Abutilon fruticosum.
Williamson — UT Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a full A. fruticosum treatment.
POWO and FNA both include Texas in the native range.

morphology.look_here_first: Gray-green subshrub, cordate velvety leaves, plain yellow flowers, and a compact cask-shaped fruit without long divergent beaks.
morphology.key_separator: Unlike A. theophrasti, it is a woody-based subshrub with smaller leaves and compact fruit; unlike A. incanum, it has more style branches and lacks the small dark-centered reflexed corolla.
